L’Algérie ouvre officiellement la concur: Algeria officially opens competition in satellite communications A call for applications for two NGSO licenses aims to bridge the digital divide and cover the entire national territory.
Alger, 09 avril 2026 – Dans le cadre de: Algiers, April 09, 2026 – As part of the national strategy to generalize telecommunications services and bridge the digital divide, the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications announces the opening of the satellite communications sector to competition. The Post and Electronic Communications Regulatory Authority (ARPCE) has launched a call for expressions of interest for the award of two licenses to establish and operate public electronic communications networks using non-geostationary orbit (NGSO) satellites.
Un bond technologique pour les zones iso: A technological leap for isolated areas This decision aims to enable operators to deploy high-speed satellite connectivity solutions in order to provide fast internet services, particularly in remote and landlocked regions that are difficult to access via traditional terrestrial infrastructure. The objective is to reduce the digital divide and ensure more uniform coverage across the entire national territory.
Diversification, concurrence et IoTL’ouv: Diversification, competition, and IoT The opening to competition pursues several complementary objectives:
Diversifier l’offre de services de commu: Diversify the range of electronic communications services;
Consacrer un accès équitable à Internet: Ensure equitable access to the internet;
Soutenir le développement de solutions I: Support the development of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions intended for structuring projects, particularly in the agriculture, mining, and transport sectors.
Déclaration du ministreDans une déclarat: Minister's statement In an official statement, Mr. Sid Ali Zerrouki, Minister of Post and Telecommunications, emphasized the importance of this breakthrough:
« Cette étape représente un moment clé d: "This step represents a key moment in strengthening Algeria's digital infrastructure, complementing existing infrastructures. It aims to bring high-speed internet services to the entire national territory, particularly in hard-to-reach areas. Through this initiative, we are working to support digital transformation and expand coverage."
Modalités pratiquesLes opérateurs intére: Practical procedures Interested operators can consult the call for applications file on the official ARPCE website. The deadline for submitting bids will be specified in the coming days. The two 15-year renewable licenses will allow the winners to operate NGSO satellite constellations to serve individuals, businesses, and local communities alike.
